SHOPPING.QUESTION: Can I repeat a saved recipe?

PRICING.TITLE: Food Diary plans: free and Premium
PRICING.DESCRIPTION: Keep your food diary manually for free. Premium adds AI recognition from photos, typed descriptions and voice, with usage allowances shown in your account.
PRICING.NEXT: Start with free manual tracking while online payments are being prepared.

FIRST.TITLE: Free manual tracking
FIRST.TEXT: Add foods and saved recipes to meals, enter portions and review calories and macros. You can continue using manual entry when AI is unavailable or you do not want to use it.

SECOND.TITLE: Premium AI recognition
SECOND.TEXT: Use a food photo, text description or voice input to prepare a meal entry. Check the identified foods, amounts and nutrients before applying the result. AI is an estimate, not a guaranteed measurement.

THIRD.TITLE: Monthly or yearly subscription
THIRD.TEXT: Monthly and yearly options are planned for Premium. Prices, renewal terms and the payment form will be published after the payment integration is connected. No payment is required to create an account and start manual tracking.

FOURTH.TITLE: Trial and usage allowances
FOURTH.TEXT: Eligible accounts can start a 7-day Premium trial without a card from the Premium section. Trial eligibility and AI usage allowances are shown in your account. Premium does not include a consultation with a nutrition professional.

PRICING.AVAILABILITY_TEXT: You can create an account and use manual tracking for free. Paid plans and prices will appear here when online payments are connected.

AI.TITLE: AI calorie tracker from photos, text and voice
AI.DESCRIPTION: Prepare a meal entry from a photo or description, then check the foods, quantities and nutrition before saving. AI recognition is available with Premium.
AI.NEXT: Prefer manual entry? You can select foods and recipes without AI on the free plan.

FIRST.TITLE: 1. Choose an input
FIRST.TEXT: Upload a food photo, type what you ate or use voice input. Include information you know, such as ingredients and quantities. A product label can help with nutrition data; a meal photo cannot show every ingredient or preparation detail.

SECOND.TITLE: 2. Review the estimate
SECOND.TEXT: Check each identified food, its amount and nutrient values. Hidden oil, sauces, cooking method and portion size can change the result. Correct anything that does not match your meal instead of saving the estimate automatically.

THIRD.TITLE: 3. Apply and save
THIRD.TEXT: Apply the reviewed result to the meal form, check its totals and save the entry. Reopen it if you need to make a later correction. Recognition prepares the data; you stay responsible for reviewing the saved record.

FOURTH.TITLE: Consent, limits and manual entry
FOURTH.TEXT: AI features require consent to processing by third-party services and a Premium allowance. Review the privacy policy and available usage in your account. If you decline AI, run out of allowance or cannot get a useful result, manual food and recipe entry remains available.

ABOUT.TITLE: A personal record of food, plans and progress
ABOUT.DESCRIPTION: Food Diary is a web application for recording meals, organizing recipes and plans, and reviewing nutrition and body measurements.
ABOUT.NEXT: Have a question about the service or your data? Contact the support address in the footer.

FIRST.TITLE: Record your own routine
FIRST.TEXT: Start with the foods and meals you actually eat. Save the recipes you use often, keep dated records and add plans or measurements when you need them. You do not have to use every section to keep a useful diary.

SECOND.TITLE: Understand the numbers
SECOND.TEXT: Nutrition totals come from the foods, recipes and quantities recorded in your account. Check product data and AI estimates before relying on them. The diary makes records available for review; it does not verify every user-entered value.

THIRD.TITLE: Choose what to share
THIRD.TEXT: Your food diary is personal. If you work with a nutrition professional, use an email invitation and choose the categories they can access. Review permissions or disconnect access when your arrangements change.

FOURTH.TITLE: Tools, not treatment
FOURTH.TEXT: Food Diary does not diagnose conditions, prescribe diets or promise weight loss. It does not provide a nutrition professional as part of a subscription. For service questions, account help or data requests, use the contact page.

CONTACT.TITLE: Contact Food Diary
CONTACT.DESCRIPTION: Ask about your account, subscription, a problem in the app or a request concerning your personal data.
CONTACT.NEXT: Write to the support address below. Do not include your password or payment card details.

FIRST.TITLE: Account and access
FIRST.TEXT: Describe what you were trying to do and the message you saw. Include the account email if it is relevant. Password reset is available from the sign-in form.

SECOND.TITLE: Subscriptions and billing
SECOND.TEXT: Include the billing period and a payment or transaction reference if you have one. The Premium section shows subscription status and available management actions. Do not send full card numbers or security codes.

THIRD.TITLE: Report an app problem
THIRD.TEXT: Include the page address, the steps that led to the issue, your browser and device, and what you expected to happen. A screenshot with private details hidden can help reproduce a visual problem.

FOURTH.TITLE: Questions about your data
FOURTH.TEXT: Use the same support address for questions about access, correction or deletion of your data. Describe the request and the account involved. See the privacy policy for information about what the service processes.

DIARY_GUIDE.TITLE: How to keep a food diary you can review
DIARY_GUIDE.DESCRIPTION: A practical guide to recording meals, quantities and notes, correcting entries and reviewing the week in Food Diary.
DIARY_GUIDE.NEXT: Start with one ordinary day. You can add plans, goals and body measurements later.

FIRST.TITLE: 1. Record the meal and date
FIRST.TEXT: Choose the date and meal type, then add the foods or saved recipe you ate. Include snacks and drinks when you want them in the record. For a breakfast with yogurt and granola, add both foods rather than a vague entry called “breakfast”. Separate entries preserve the quantities and nutrition behind the meal.

SECOND.TITLE: 2. Check quantities and units
SECOND.TEXT: Check whether the food data is given per 100 g, per serving or for another base amount. Enter the amount eaten in the matching unit. Half a package is not necessarily one serving: use the label or a measured amount when available. If AI prepared the entry, review food names, portions and nutrient values before applying it.

THIRD.TITLE: 3. Save useful notes and correct mistakes
THIRD.TEXT: A note can preserve a recipe change or a detail you want to discuss later. Save the meal, then reopen it to check the record. If you find the wrong date, food or quantity, edit the entry and review the updated totals. Keep notes factual and useful for you; the diary does not need to be a judgement on the meal.

FOURTH.TITLE: 4. Review several days
FOURTH.TEXT: Use meal history and Statistics to review a period. Check whether repeated meals have consistent quantities and whether missing food data affects totals. A weekly check-in can hold your observations and next steps. If you work with a nutrition professional, share only the categories you want them to review. Records show what was entered; they do not establish a medical conclusion.

RECIPE_GUIDE.TITLE: How to record calories in a homemade meal
RECIPE_GUIDE.DESCRIPTION: Keep ingredients, the finished recipe and the portion eaten consistent. A worked example explains why servings and cooked weight matter.
RECIPE_GUIDE.NEXT: The numbers here are a calculation example, not a recommended meal or calorie target. Check the data for your own ingredients.

FIRST.TITLE: 1. Record the ingredients used
FIRST.TEXT: Use the nutrition data and quantities for the actual ingredients, including oil or sauce that goes into the dish. Check whether each value describes a raw or cooked food. Do not use dry-weight nutrition for a cooked-weight quantity without accounting for the difference. Missing ingredients or incompatible units make the recipe total less useful.

SECOND.TITLE: 2. Check the finished recipe and servings
SECOND.TEXT: Cooking changes the finished weight, particularly when water is absorbed or lost. Keep the recipe’s nutrition basis clear: a complete batch, a serving or a stated weight. Decide how many servings the saved recipe represents and check their nutrition. If the batch changes, review the saved recipe before reusing it.

THIRD.TITLE: 3. A worked portion example
THIRD.TEXT: Suppose a finished dish weighs 600 g and its checked total is 900 kcal, 60 g protein, 20 g fat and 120 g carbs. If the dish is evenly mixed, a 150 g portion is one quarter: 225 kcal, 15 g protein, 5 g fat and 30 g carbs. Water changed the weight, but this example’s total nutrients came from the ingredients. These are illustrative values, not food database values.

FOURTH.TITLE: 4. Save the amount you ate
FOURTH.TEXT: Select the saved recipe in a meal and enter the servings eaten. Check the resulting nutrition before saving. In the example, a recipe saved as four equal servings would be logged as one serving for 150 g. If a serving or recipe definition differs, use that definition instead. Correct a saved entry when the food or amount does not match what you ate.
